Ajay Garg & Ors. Cnr No. Dlsh03-000171-2022 In the matter of: 1. Sonia Verma, W/o Sh. Rajeev Verma, 2. Rajeev Verma, S/o Late Sh. Shamsher Singh Verma, Both R/o H. No. 94/4A, Street No. 1, East Azad Nagar, Delhi-110051. ........Plaintiffs Versus 1. Ajay Garg, S/o Sh. Janeshwer Garg, At: Shree Balaji Snakes, Plot No. 469/B/1A/4, Shop No. 3, Shalimar Park, Bhola Nath Nagar, Shahdara, Delhi-110032. 2. Station House Officer (Sho), Police Station Frash Bazar, Shalimar Park, Bhola Nath Nagar, Shahdara, Delhi-110032. 3. East Delhi Municipal Corporation, Through Commissioner, Edmc, 419, Udhyog Sadan, Patparganj Industrial Area, Delhi-110092. ........ Defendants Digitally signed by Mayank Mayank Goel Goel Date: 2024.02.07 ________________________________________________ _ _ _ _ 14:01:11 +0530 Civil Suit No. 124/2022
texts.facts: The brief facts are narrated by the plaintiffs are that the plaintiffs are residing at House No 94/4A, Street No.1, East Azad Nagar, Delhi with their family. That the plaintiffs are also owner of the property bearing Plot No. 469/B/1A/4, Shalimar Park, Bhola Nath Nagar, Shahdara, Delhi and the defendant no.1 is one of the tenant of shop No.3 in the above mentioned property i.e. the suit property which is shown in Red Colour in the Site Plan attached with the plaint. That the defendant No.1 is the tenant of the plaintiffs and he use the tenanted premises to selling the raw material of chemicals but in these days the defendant no.1 change his trade and use the tenanted premises i.e. the shop in question for food items without obtaining the Health and trade license from the defendant No.3. That the defendant no.1 also encroach the area of footpath for preparation of foods i.e. tandoor, Momos stall, chaap counter and sitting chairs tables etc. with the help of the employees of defendant no.2 and defendant no.3. That the customers of defendant no. 1 also using the abovesaid area and foothpath area for consuming alcohol, etc till late hours and also threw garbage on the road. That the when the plaintiff objected the same, the defendant no. 1 gave threat to plaintiff no.2 to face the dire consequences. That the plaintiff no. 2 gave the written complaint to the official of the defendant no.3 but till date the official of the defendant No. 3 did not take any legal action against the defendant no.1 qua the illegal running the food shop and encroach the footpath M A Y A N K b y M A Y A N K G O E L G O E L D a t e : 2 0 2 4 . 0 2 . 0 7 AJAY GARG & ORS . Page No. 2 of 12 CNR NO. DLSH03-000171-2022 to establish the Tandoor, Momos stall and siting area chairs and tables where serve the food to the customers. That 2-3 person who claim himself the local sweeper of the area and another the license/food/Health officer of the locality. That they have given threat to the plaintiff no.2, says "TUJHE SAMJANA PADEGA TUM HAMARI BADHA DAAL RAHA HAI TUJHE YAHA KAAM NAHI KARNA HAI KYA YAHA KA SARA KUDA TERI DUKAN KE AAGE DALEGE TUB TUJHE PTA CHALEGA KI HAMARI TAKAAT KYA HAI, YAHA SE UPPER TAK KA HISAB HOTA HAI OR POLICE BHI HAMARE SATH HAI". That on 01.12.2021, the plaintiff no.2 also gave the written complaint through speed post to the defendant no.2 but till date no action taken by the official of the defendant no.2 against the illegal activity done by the defendant no.1. That the plaintiffs have also filed the suit against defendant no. 1 for eviction and eviction order has been passed in the said case. Hence, the present suit has been filed by the plaintiffs for decree of permanent injunction in favour of the plaintiffs and against the defendants, their employees, agents, servants, relatives, legal heirs and representatives, from restraining them from creating any illegal encroachment on footpath and for not running his shop without the proper Health & Trade License by the concerned authority in the suit property/shop in question i.e. Shop No. 3 in Property bearing no. 469/B/1A/4, Shop No. 3, Shalimar Park, Bholanath Nagar, Shahdara, Delhi-110032, as shown in the Red Colour in the Site Plan. The plaintiffs also sought the decree of mandatory injunctions in favour of plaintiffs and against the defendants for directions to remove tandoor, momos stall and Sonia Verma vs Ajay Garg on 7 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104065303/ 2 other articles which are lying on footpath in front of the suit property and further directions to defendant no. 2 to immediately stop the illegal work which was run by defendant no. 1 in MAYANK b y M A Y A N K G O E L G O E L D a t e : 2 0 2 4 . 0 2 . 0 7 ____________________________________________________ 14:01:27 +0530 SONIA VERMA & ORS. VS. AJAY GARG & ORS. Page No. 3 of 12 CNR NO. DLSH03-000171-2022 the suit property/shop in question i.e. Shop No. 3 in Property bearing no. 469/B/1A/4, Shop No. 3, Shalimar Park, Bholanath Nagar, Shahdara, Delhi-110032, as shown in the Red Colour in the Site Plan. 2. Summons of the suit were issued to the defendants. However, written statement was filed only by defendant no. 1 and 3. 3. In the Written Statement, the defendant no. 1 has taken certain preliminary objections that the plaintiffs have no cause of action to file the present suit. The defendant no. 1 denied all the averments made in the plaint and stated that the defendant no. 1 previously used to run a business of Tour & Travels but due to Covid- 19, the said business came to an end and the plaintiff had to change his business from Tour and Travels to Fast Food Shop for survival of his family members. That the defendant also has a license of FSSAI and Trade License for selling the food items. That the plaintiffs have not approached the court with clean hands and suppressed the material facts. Thats the plaintiffs themselves encroached the footpath area by allowing daily hawkers for keeping stalls/food rehri in front of the shops of the suit property and taking daily charges to the tune of Rs.300/- to Rs. 500/- from the said hawkers/rehri. That the defendant had never encroached the area of the footpath as alleged in the plaint. Hence, the suit of the plaintiff shall be dismissed. 4. In the Written Statement, the defendant no. 3/MCD has taken certain preliminary objections that the present suit is barred u/s 477/478 of the DMC Act, 1957 for want of service of statutory notice prior to filing of the suit and the plaintiffs have no cause of action against the defendant no. 3. Page No. 4 of 12 CNR NO. DLSH03-000171-2022 that the raid was conducted in the suit property on 14.03.2022 by the area Food Hygiene Inspector of Public Health Department by Truck No. DL-1LN-3307 alongwith Driver and Food Hygiene Staff of Shahdara South Zone and all the items which were seized during the raid has already been deposited in the Municipal Food Hygiene Store, Shastri Park, Delhi. Hence, the suit of the plaintiffs shall be dismissed. 5. No replication has been filed by the plaintiffs to the WS of defendant no. 1 and 3. 6. PW-1 was not cross-examined by defendants despite opportunity being given. Thereafter, PE stands closed.
texts.arguments: For the same, I may gainfully referred to the observation made by Hon'ble Apex Court in "Anvar P.V. Vs. P.K. Basheer & Ors, 2014 SCC Online SC 732 " that any documentary evidence by way of Electronic record under the Evidence Act, in view of Section 59 and 65A, can be proved only in accordance with the procedure prescribed under Section 65B. In the case titled as "Somi Atamananda Vs. Siri Ram Kumar Tapobana, 2005 10 SCC 51, the expression 'cause of action' has been defined to me every fact, which if traversed it would be necessary for plaintiff to prove in order to support his right to the judgment of the court, though, it does not comprise every piece of evidence which is necessary to be proved. Section 477 of The Delhi Municipal Corporation Act, 1957 provides for protection of action of a Corporation, etc. and lays down that :- "No suit or prosecution shall be entertained in any court against a Corporation or against any municipal authority or against any municipal officer or other municipal employee or against any person acting under the order or direction of any municipal authority or any municipal officer or other municipal employee, for anything, which in good faith done or intended to be done, under this Act or any rule, regulation or bye-law made thereunder." Section 478 of The Delhi Municipal Corporation Act, 1957 provides for notice to be given of the suits and lays down that :- "(1) No suit shall be instituted against a Corporation or against any municipal authority or against any municipal officer or other municipal employee or against any person acting under the order or direction of any municipal authority or any municipal officer or other municipal employee, in respect of any act done, or purporting to have been done in pursuance of this Act or any rule, regulation or bye-law made thereunder until the expiration of two months after notice in writing has been left at the municipal office and in case of such officer or employee or person, unless notice in writing has not been delivered to him or left at his office or place of residence, and unless such notice states explicitly the cause of MAYANK MAYANK G O E L G O E L D a t e : 2 0 2 4 . 0 2 . 0 7 1 4 : 0 2 : 1 6 + 0 5 3 0 ____________________________________________________ SONIA VERMA & ORS. VS. AJAY GARG & ORS. Page No. 10 of 12 CNR NO. DLSH03-000171-2022 action, the nature of the relief sought, the amount of compensation claimed, and the name and place of residence of the intending plaintiff, and unless the plaint contains a statement that such notice has been so left and delivered. (2) No suit, such as is described in sub-section(1), shall unless it is a suit for the recovery of immovable property or for a declaration of title thereto, be instituted after Sonia Verma vs Ajay Garg on 7 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104065303/ 7 the expiry of six months from the date on which the cause of action arises. (3) Nothing in sub-section (1) shall be deemed to apply to a suit in which the only relief claimed is an injunction of which the object would be defeated by the giving of notice or the postponement of the institution of the suit."
